title: Towards a Theory of Learnability via Debate
abstract: arXiv:2611.17303v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Debate has been recently proposed as a training protocol that is hoped to produce more aligned models even as model capabilities scale. The idea is that the human, instead of providing supervision in the form of labels, judges a debate between two models that compete to prove the correctness of opposite labels. It can be shown that functions of a much higher computational complexity can be correctly judged in this way, compared to the complexity of functions that can be directly evaluated using a computationally weak evaluator. This suggests that perhaps debate can be used to teach very complicated functions to models. However, previous work has largely ignored the fact that this is a training protocol, and simply analyzes the game being played between the two debaters for a known judge. We take the first steps towards understanding the learning problem implicit within the protocol, by formulating it as an online learning problem. We

translated_title: 迈向基于辩论的可学习性理论
translated_abstract: 辩论（Debate）最近被提出作为一种训练协议，其目标是即使模型能力不断扩展，也能产生更加对齐的模型。其核心思想是：人类不再以标签的形式提供监督，而是评判两个模型之间的辩论——这两个模型竞相证明相反标签的正确性。可以证明，与计算能力较弱的评估器能够直接评估的函数复杂度相比，通过这种方式可以正确评判计算复杂度高得多的函数。这表明，辩论或许可以用来向模型教授非常复杂的函数。然而，以往的工作在很大程度上忽略了这实际上是一种训练协议这一事实，而只是简单地分析了在评判者已知的情况下两个辩论者之间所进行的博弈。我们通过将该协议形式化为一个在线学习问题，迈出了理解其中隐含的学习问题的第一步。
tldr: 该论文首次将辩论训练协议形式化为在线学习问题，迈出了理解辩论作为训练方法所隐含的学习问题的第一步。
en_tdlr: This paper takes the first steps toward understanding the learning problem implicit in the debate training protocol by formulating it as an online learning problem.
